title: Geometric component counts commute with base change
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. For $s\in S$, let $n_f(s)\in\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$ be the number of maximal nonempty connected subsets [def-weil-connected-scheme] of $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$, where $K$ is any algebraically closed extension of the residue field $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field] [def-weil-algebraic-closure]; an infinite number is recorded as $\infty$, and the empty fibre has count $0$. This number is independent of $K$. For every morphism $g:T\to S$, put $f_T:X\times_ST\to T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $n_{f_T}(t)=n_f(g(t))$ for every $t\in T$.

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$ and algebraically closed extensions $K_1,K_2$ of $\kappa(s)$. By [lem-weil-common-extension-fields] choose embeddings $K_1\to M\leftarrow K_2$ agreeing over $\kappa(s)$. Every nonconstant separable polynomial over $K_i$ has a root by [def-weil-algebraic-closure], so $K_i$ is separably closed by [def-pc-separably-closed]. By [def-pc-fibre-product], $(X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K_i)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K_i}\operatorname{Spec}M$ is canonically isomorphic to $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}M$: both represent pairs of maps to $X$ and $\operatorname{Spec}M$ agreeing over $S$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sepclosed-field-components-bijection] over each $K_i$. Thus the same $M$-scheme has component bijections to both geometric fibres. Compose one bijection with the inverse of the other. The finite counts agree, or both component sets are infinite. For empty fibres both component sets are empty and the count is zero. This proves independence of $K$.

Fix $t\in T$ and $s=g(t)$. The residue-field map [def-weil-residue-field] is $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(t)$, a field embedding. Choose algebraically closed extensions $K/\kappa(s)$ and $K'/\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Apply [lem-weil-common-extension-fields] over $\kappa(s)$, regarding $K'$ as an extension through $\kappa(t)$, to choose embeddings $K\to M\leftarrow K'$ agreeing on $\kappa(s)$. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $((X\times_ST)\times_T\operatorname{Spec}K')\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K'}\operatorname{Spec}M\cong X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}M$: a map to either side is exactly a pair of maps to $X$ and $\operatorname{Spec}M$ agreeing over $S$, since the map to $T$ is forced by $\operatorname{Spec}M\to\operatorname{Spec}K'\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to T$. The same universal property gives $(X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\operatorname{Spec}M\cong X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}M$.

Every nonconstant separable polynomial over $K$ or $K'$ is nonconstant, hence has a root by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]; thus both fields are separably closed by [def-pc-separably-closed]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sepclosed-field-components-bijection] to $M/K$ and $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$, and to $M/K'$ and $(X\times_ST)\times_T\operatorname{Spec}K'$. The source schemes of the two projections are canonically isomorphic by step 2, so their component sets are in bijection: the isomorphism and its inverse are continuous, send nonempty connected subsets to nonempty connected subsets, and therefore send maximal such subsets to maximal such subsets. Composing these bijections gives equal component counts for the two geometric fibres, including zero and infinity. Independence from the algebraically closed extensions was proved in step 1; these counts are therefore $n_f(s)$ and $n_{f_T}(t)$. This proves $n_{f_T}(t)=n_f(g(t))$.

lean.statement: theorem geometricComponentCount_baseChange {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : (∀ (s : S) (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [IsAlgClosed K] [IsAlgClosed L] (i : S.residueField s ⟶ CommRingCat.of K) (j : S.residueField s ⟶ CommRingCat.of L), ENat.card (ConnectedComponents (pullback f (Spec.map i ≫ S.fromSpecResidueField s) : Scheme.{u})) = ENat.card (ConnectedComponents (pullback f (Spec.map j ≫ S.fromSpecResidueField s) : Scheme.{u}))) ∧ (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : T ⟶ S) (t : T) (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [IsAlgClosed K] [IsAlgClosed L] (i : S.residueField (g t) ⟶ CommRingCat.of K) (j : T.residueField t ⟶ CommRingCat.of L), ENat.card (ConnectedComponents (pullback (pullback.snd f g) (Spec.map j ≫ T.fromSpecResidueField t) : Scheme.{u})) = ENat.card (ConnectedComponents (pullback f (Spec.map i ≫ S.fromSpecResidueField (g t)) : Scheme.{u})))
